location: Design Notes > Worker interface ("Parseable = a JSON object with those keys and engine = the worker's, whatever the exit code" vs "a worker that exits 143 or by a signal while the version process was not stopped is a crash")
issue: These two rules conflict when a worker has already written a valid result file and then exits 143 or by a signal while the version process was not stopped. Examples: SIGKILL from the OOM killer during Playwright/interpreter shutdown, a SIGTERM that lands after `os.replace`, or a stray signal. The first rule says to use the result. The second says the cell is `crash`. Neither rule says which one wins.
implementation_impact: The implementer has to pick an order: check the exit code first, or check that the result parses first. One order turns a fully driven cell (possibly a `fail` with conclusive findings) into `inconclusive` `crash`, which hides a blocking failure and feeds Plan step 3 `blocked-infra`. The other order keeps it. The unit tests for the Worker crash row will then encode whichever order was picked.
suggestion: State the precedence explicitly. For example: a parseable result always wins, whatever the exit code or signal. The 143/signal rule applies only when no parseable result exists, and decides only whether the cell is `crash` or skipped under the stop path. Add a unit case: result written, then exit -9.

location: Design Notes > Worker interface (spec.json carries both `ctx` and a top-level `screenshot_dir`); Always > Child (screenshots in `<shots>/<ver>/<engine>`)
issue: Today's version `ctx` already contains `screenshot_dir` = `<shots>/<ver>` (ps-e2e-run.py `_run_one_version_inner`), and `_snap` reads `ctx['screenshot_dir']`. spec.json serialises that `ctx` and also has a separate top-level `screenshot_dir` (`<shots>/<ver>/<engine>`). The spec doesn't say the worker must overwrite `ctx['screenshot_dir']` with the top-level value. It also doesn't say what the worker does when the best-effort mkdir of `<ver>/<engine>` failed: null, or fall back to `<ver>`.
implementation_impact: If the worker passes `ctx` through unchanged, parallel screenshots land flat in `<ver>/`. Both engines then write into one folder, contradicting the contract's per-engine subdir and the rewritten SKILL.md/quickstart paths. Visual review would then look in `<ver>/<engine>/` and find nothing.
suggestion: Either drop `screenshot_dir` from the serialised `ctx` and keep only the top-level key, or state that the worker sets `ctx['screenshot_dir']` from the top-level key, which is null when the version process failed to create the subdir (screenshots skipped, as today).

location: Code Map / Tasks > ps-flashlight-run.py (`progress_attach(path, version)`); Design Notes > Worker interface (spec.json `slow_after`, worker registers under the Job ID)
issue: spec.json carries `slow_after`, but the specified helper `fl.progress_attach(path, version)` has no parameter for it. `progress_init` is forbidden in workers, and `phase._beat` reads `_PROGRESS['slow_after']`. The spec also leaves the order of `progress_attach` and `job_register` open. `job_register` snapshots `_PROGRESS['path']` into the registry entry (`progress_file`) at registration time, and needs `module`/`layer`/`versions`, which spec.json does not carry by name.
implementation_impact: A literal implementation silently ignores the operator's `--slow-after` in workers, so `browser:<engine>`, the longest phase, uses the 180 s default. Registering before attaching leaves `progress_file: null` in the workers' registry entries, which `--list-jobs` shows. The implementer also has to guess the module name for `job_register`, for example from `ctx['mod']`.
suggestion: Specify `progress_attach(path, version, slow_after)`, or say that it also sets `_PROGRESS['slow_after']`. State the worker start order (set `fl.RUN_ID`, `progress_attach`, `job_register(job_id, module=ctx['mod'], layer='e2e', versions=version)`, `timing_activate`), or add `module` to spec.json.

location: Always > Child, bullet 2 (`LOCK_EX` when the scenario 'has a BO `goto`', else `LOCK_SH`); contract Cross-engine lock (`_needs_bo` per scenario)
issue: BO is detected only by `goto` with `area: "bo"`. `_resolve_url` also accepts `url` (for example `{bo}/index.php?controller=AdminOrders`) with no area, and `discover_scenarios` accepts such specs without a note. A spec that reaches the back office through `url` is classed FO-only, so it takes `LOCK_SH` and runs on both engines at once against BO state.
implementation_impact: The implementer builds exactly what is written. On such a module, the headline guarantee ('a BO scenario can never overlap, and so never mask, another engine's scenario') is silently false, and live test (c) cannot catch it because its BO-scenario set uses the same classifier. Masked failures then pass unless a finding triggers a rerun.
suggestion: Either classify a scenario as BO when any `goto` resolves under `ctx['bo']` (the area or a `url` beginning with `{bo}`/the admin path), or have `discover_scenarios` emit a scenario note for a `url` goto into the admin path with no `area: bo`, so such a spec drops `ready` instead of silently weakening the lock. If this changes the contract, it is Ask First.

location: Code Map (`_drive_page`/`drive_engine` -- per-scenario hook, spans); Design Notes > `scenario_spans` (worker: lock + spans + marker; in-process first pass: spans only; sequential passes: none)
issue: `drive_engine` and `_drive_page` must behave three ways depending on the pass. Worker passes take the lock, hold the holder marker, record spans and write step markers. The in-process first pass (single engine or sequential fallback) records spans only. `rerun-seq` and BO-login fallback passes do none of these. The spec names no seam for selecting the mode (a new parameter, a hook object, or a ctx key). `ctx` is serialised into spec.json and copied per scenario.
implementation_impact: Putting the mode in `ctx` leaks it into spec.json and the per-scenario `local` dicts, and invites in-process passes to inherit a worker flag. Forgetting to disable spans in sequential passes lets the rerun overwrite the lockstep `scenario_spans`, which the merge rule and live test (c) rely on. The stub tests ("lock and barrier with real flock/files across threads") also need a seam to inject.
suggestion: Name the seam. For example, `drive_engine(engine, scenarios, ctx, headed=False, hook=None)`, where `hook` is an object with `before(k, scenario)` and `after(k, scenario)`. The worker passes a LockstepHook, the in-process first pass a SpanHook, and sequential passes None. Spans are returned in the result and never stored in `ctx`.

location: Tasks > ps-e2e-run.py ('worker timings re-recorded into the version sink in order so suffixes continue'); Design Notes > Phases (`browser:<engine>#2` for the BO-login fallback); I/O row BO-login fallback
issue: The spec says worker timings are re-recorded into the version sink, but not when relative to the sequential passes. Suffixes are assigned by order of `TimingSink.record` calls. The worker's lockstep `browser:firefox` must therefore be recorded before the fallback pass's `browser:firefox` for the fallback to become `#2`. Likewise, the worker's `lock-wait`/`barrier-wait` entries must be recorded before any in-process phase of the same engine.
implementation_impact: An implementer who collects worker results at reap time but re-records timings while assembling cells at the end (after the confirmation passes) gets the fallback as bare `browser:firefox` and the discarded lockstep pass as `browser:firefox#2`. This inverts which duration the I/O row and docs call the counting pass. `_engine_failed`-style mid-run reads of the sink would also see no lockstep phase.
suggestion: State that each worker's timings are re-recorded when that worker is reaped (or all of them right after the last reap), and always before the first sequential pass.
